description: Quetzal Germany is a macroscopic passenger-transport model configured for Germany. Its README links a method paper and describes a four-step workflow with demand zones, public transport and road networks, trip generation, origin-destination matrices, mode choice, route assignment and energy or emissions post-processing. Users provide scenario parameters and source network or demand data; outputs are travel volumes and transport-system indicators for the configured case. Geographic coverage is Germany. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing for the code. The README says some calibration stages require access to calibration data, so a public run may not reproduce the published fit exactly. A limitation is that a national model depends on its network vintage, survey data and behavioural assumptions. It can test passenger-demand and modal-shift scenarios for transport infrastructure. The related catalogue AequilibraE model is a different transport modelling platform. No model input, output or notebook was downloaded.
inputs: German networks, travel zones, demand data and scenario parameters
name: Quetzal Germany passenger transport model
notes: G7 G7-1806. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. Full recalibration requires external survey or calibration data identified by the README.
outputs: Trip demand, route assignment, energy and emissions indicators
